links.title: Funnel of Thoughts: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Early Voting and Rollout Pruning

evidence: Section 4.1: FoT@32 and SC@32 return the same correctness outcome on 3,580 of 3,600 paired model-problem instances (12 FoT wins, 8 losses), not significant under McNemar's exact test (p=0.50), bootstrap CI [-0.14,+0.36] pp.
Table 2: across 6 models x 4 math benchmarks, FoT@32 averages 94.5 accuracy vs SC@32's 94.4 with 50.7% average attention-FLOP saving; per-cell savings range ~33-60%.

Table 7 (Section 4.5): two-by-two ablation shows random pruning loses accuracy (-0.42) at similar compute savings while hesitation-density pruning preserves SC@32 (94.61 without early voting), isolating the lexical signal as the operative mechanism.
Section 4.4 / Table 6: online SGLang deployment on a single A100 with DS-R1-7B on 30 AIME24 problems: FoT@32 solves 24/30 vs SC@32's 23/30, wall time -37.6%, attention FLOPs -56.1%.

Section 4.2 / Table 4: unchanged configuration transfers to four held-out models (Qwen3-14B/32B, Skywork-OR1-7B, Phi-4-reasoning), aggregate +0.6pp with 51.9% average FLOP saving; Section 4.3 / Table 5 shows GPQA-Diamond +1.3pp and LCB-Lite +1.42pp mean pass rate with pass@32 -2.8pp.

Section 6 Limitations: evaluation restricted to extractable-answer tasks, calibration pool has MATH500 supplying 3,000 of 3,600 pairs, English-only marker kernel and fixed checkpoints; Appendix D.2 quantifies savings degrading from 48.7% to 23.0% under linear attention.

Appendix D.1: generation uses SGLang with T=0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 30, max 32,768 tokens, seed 42+rep_id; grading moved from exact match to math_verify with effects disclosed; Table 8 lists the full 21-marker kernel with point-biserial statistics.
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM reasoning-efficiency work squarely within scope: a training-free test-time scaling method (early voting + hesitation-marker-density pruning) that matches SC@32 accuracy at roughly half attention FLOPs across six LRMs, directly serving the high-weight reasoning/CoT, LLM, scaling-efficiency, and inference-serving preferences. Novelty is moderate: the lexical 'Wait/Actually/perhaps' signal is simple and adjacent to prior keyword-suppression and budget-forcing work; the distinct contribution is pool-level relative density ranking plus vote banking, and the demonstrated Pareto point rather than a new modeling technique. Rigor is unusually strong: 115,200 rollouts, pre-registered baselines (Adaptive Consistency, Slim-SC, DSC, Certaindex proxy), a 340-configuration hyperparameter sweep, a 2x2 mechanism ablation showing random pruning loses accuracy while density pruning does not (Table 7), kernel-size robustness, and significance testing (McNemar p=0.50, bootstrap CI) with honest reporting of non-significant accuracy deltas and three coexisting FLOP accountings. Evidence is mostly well supported, though most results are offline simulations of a pre-generated pool and the online deployment (Table 6) covers only 30 problems on one model; the calibration pool is admittedly MATH500-dominated. Generalization is demonstrated on four held-out models and two out-of-domain tasks with an unchanged configuration, but is scoped to English, extractable-answer tasks and large pools (k>=16-24), and savings degrade to 23.0% under linear attention (Appendix D.2). Reproducibility is good: generation parameters, seeds, the full 21-marker kernel, checkpoint schedules, and baseline configurations are disclosed, but no explicit code-release claim is made.

primary_link.title: Funnel of Thoughts: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Early Voting and Rollout Pruning

radar.summary: Large Reasoning Models produce diverse, sometimes inconsistent answers across repeated queries on the same problem, so multi-sample inference is a prerequisite for reliable deployment. Majority voting at k rollouts is the standard solution and the de facto accuracy target for this regime, but it is prohibitively expensive at the scale LRMs require. We introduce Funnel of Thoughts (FoT), an inference-time method that preserves the full 32-trajectory voted accuracy while halving its attention FLOP
radar.summary_zh: 大型推理模型（LRM）對同一問題重複取樣時，答案常多樣且不一致，因此以 Self-Consistency（SC@k）多數決投票作為可靠部署的標準做法，但每條軌跡都須完整生成，注意力計算量隨序列長度平方成長，在 LRM 規模下成本高昂。本文分析 6 個 LRM 在 AIME24/25、AMC23 與 MATH500 上共 115,200 條推理軌跡，發現錯誤與無答案軌跡僅佔約 9.5%，卻消耗不成比例的運算，且其文本中猶豫標記（如 Wait、Actually、perhaps）密度顯著偏高，與正確性呈負相關。作者據此提出 Funnel of Thoughts（FoT）：在固定 token 數檢查點執行兩項機制——早期投票先將已承諾答案的軌跡存入票庫，軌跡剪枝則依密度排名移除最無生產力的少數，全程不需訓練、獎勵模型或 logit 存取。結果顯示 FoT@32 在維持 SC@32 準確率的同時，節省約一半注意力 FLOPs（全模型 FLOP 減少 28.8%），線上部署時整體耗時亦降低 37.6%，且相同設定可直接轉移到未調校的模型與 GPQA、程式碼生成等跨領域任務。限制包括僅適用於可抽取最終答案的任務、取樣池過小（k<16）時剪枝可能有害，以及猶豫標記核心與答案承諾偵測皆以英文情境為主，且在高效率注意力機制下節省幅度會縮減。其價值在於以零成本的詞彙訊號，大幅降低測試時擴展的運算門檻。
radar.title: Funnel of Thoughts: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Early Voting and Rollout Pruning
radar.title_zh: Funnel of Thoughts：透過早期投票與軌跡剪枝實現高效率測試時擴展

links.title: Beyond the Editing Canvas: Evidence Divergence in OOXML-to-LLM Ingestion

evidence: Abstract: confirms 21 evidence forks across Excel/Word/PowerPoint; 13-tool extraction panel all emit at least one fork; four APIs return the trap in 48-76% of trials across 8,400 runs.
§3.2: workflow quantified - 639 candidate records, 542 runnable fixtures, 412 pass Gate 1 (Office oracle), 163 pass Gate 2 (extraction panel), dedup/scope screening yields 21 mechanisms.
§4.1 Response Labeling: Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 label all 8,400 API responses with 100% raw agreement; 420-sample human audit agrees with all automated verdicts.
§4.1 Controls: 0/840 matched-clean twin trials surface the trap; 24/24 visible-positive document-API trials succeed, bounding the main condition.

§4.3: mean record-level propagation ranges 0.48 (GLM) to 0.76 (Kimi) across APIs and 0.52-0.76 across web chatbots; 20 of 21 mechanisms asserted by at least one interface; 98.3% of 840 document-API pairs produce identical verdicts across ten repetitions.

§4.4 Table 6: Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, and Opus 4.8 share one published ingestion path (openpyxl/pandoc/markitdown) and expose the identical 16/21 mechanism set, supporting the ingestion-path-over-model claim.
§4.6: 748 of 4,263 documents (17.5%) carry at least one structural signature; five common signatures occur at 2.75-16.5% base rates, limiting presence-only screening.
Discussion and Limitations: acknowledges mechanism-balanced rates are not population estimates and that tool/service results are pinned-configuration snapshots.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A security measurement study squarely on LLM methodology: how OOXML-to-LLM ingestion (RAG loaders, agent pipelines, native file-input APIs) selects evidence, with a threat model, defenses discussion, and evaluation of live LLM services. Strongly matches LLM, RAG, agents, AI safety, and evaluation preferences; not a pure domain application. Novelty is solid but incremental over prior PDF render/extract divergence and DOCX hidden-carrier studies; the spec-grounded mining, cross-format catalog (21 mechanisms, six-dimension taxonomy), and behavior-level matching of closed ingestion paths are the new contributions. Rigor is high: systematic spec KB mining (639 candidates) with empirical two-gate confirmation to 21 mechanisms, pinned 13-tool extraction panel, 8,400 API + 1,470 web trials, dual judges with human audit, and benign-twin/visible-positive controls that bound the effect. Evidence is quantitative and internally consistent, though judged by LLMs (100% agreement is unusually clean), rates are mechanism-balanced rather than population estimates (acknowledged), and vendor results are config snapshots. Generalizability is moderate: method transfers to other formats, but exposure vectors are pinned-version findings. Reproducibility is decent (pinned versions, builder programs, named datasets, appendix prompts) but live web services and the LLM mining stage limit exact replication, and no explicit artifact URL is given in the provided text.

primary_link.title: Beyond the Editing Canvas: Evidence Divergence in OOXML-to-LLM Ingestion

radar.summary: LLM pipelines increasingly ingest Office Open XML (OOXML) documents (Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files) as first-class evidence in financial, compliance, and retrieval-augmented workflows, implicitly assuming semantic integrity: that the evidence consumed by the model matches the content shown in the Microsoft Office suite editing canvas. We show that this assumption can fail in OOXML-to-LLM pipelines. The same specification-valid OOXML file can yield one evidentiary view in Microsoft Office and
radar.summary_zh: LLM 管線常將 Word、Excel、PowerPoint 等 OOXML 文件匯入為模型證據，並假設模型所見與使用者在 Office 編輯畫布看到的內容一致。本文指出此語意完整性假設可能失效：同一份符合規格的檔案，在 Office 與擷取管線會呈現不同內容，形成「多重事實」，作者將引發分歧的規格內建構造命名為「證據分叉」。團隊把 ECMA-376 與微軟擴充規格建成知識庫，以 LLM 探勘出 639 個候選，經最小檔案實例化，以 Office 截圖與 13 種擷取工具雙重驗證，確認 21 個證據分叉，涵蓋表示、狀態、可見性、相容性、範圍與線性化六個維度。以 TAT-QA 財報片段製作的 210 份帶陷阱文件，測試 4 個原生匯入 API 與 7 個網頁聊天機器人：8,400 次 API 試驗中 48%–76% 的回應把陷阱當成文件事實，20/21 個機制至少被一個介面外洩。暴露程度取決於匯入路徑與擷取器版本而非模型：同一供應商的 API 與網頁入口行為各異，三個 Claude 模型共用同一份文件 skill 時暴露集合完全相同。對 16 個開源 RAG 專案的調查顯示，預設匯入路徑集中於少數擷取器家族；一般文件的結構特徵出現基率呈雙峰分布，僅憑存在與否難以篩檢常見通道。限制是機制均衡的評測集不代表部署分布，結果僅反映特定版本組態。本文凸顯擷取器選擇即是安全政策：安全匯入需明確契約，並保留證據來源與語意角色。
radar.title: Beyond the Editing Canvas: Evidence Divergence in OOXML-to-LLM Ingestion
radar.title_zh: 超越編輯畫布：OOXML 至 LLM 匯入流程的證據分歧

links.title: Auditing and Decomposing Feedback-Driven Evolution in LLM Test Generation under the Oracle Problem

evidence: Abstract: 'On external inputs where three accepted implementations agree, generated outputs match the panel only 27.79% and 50.12% of the time. A single reference inflates the apparent evolutionary gain by 9.46–14.85 percentage points; after audit, equal-budget independent resampling is 6.01–18.83 points better.'

Section 3.1 / Table 1: 'The external cohort was hash-locked before fresh generation from TestCase-Eval: 114 non-interactive tasks'; models are 'Qwen2.5-Coder-7B Instruct' and 'the released Qwen3.5-9B checkpoint with thinking disabled'.

Section 3.5 (Inference and integrity): 'External programs run in bubblewrap namespaces with time, memory, process, and output limits... Model artifacts, cohorts, folds, generated rows, analyses, and paper summaries are linked by SHA-256 locks.'

Table 5 / Section 4.2: gain inflation intervals '9.46–14.85 pp across all four conditions... with every 95% interval strictly above zero'; Table 6: 'Matched exceeds Evolve by 18.83 and 9.72 pp on development and by 10.91 and 6.01 pp externally'.

Table 10 / Section 4.6: 'Real–Placebo is much smaller: +1.99 pp [+0.08, +3.88] and +0.28 pp [−1.41, +2.03]... Both model-specific decisions are inconclusive'; Table 11: yield-matched replay gives '−0.30 and +0.78 pp, both with zero-crossing intervals'.

Section 4.5 / Table 8: blinded audit with '91.67% exact agreement and Cohen's κ=.823'; 'Overall, 94.41% (95% CI [91.85, 96.51]) are jointly judged invalid, while 3.60% [2.23, 5.14] are jointly judged valid.'
Section 7 (External validity): 'Both model conditions are from the Qwen family... they neither establish cross-family generality nor identify a scale effect'; all tasks algorithmic and Python-family.

Data Availability: 'An anonymized replication package containing protocol locks, task-level derived metrics, analysis code... is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/llm-test-evolution-audit-8CF5/.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: An LLM-methodology audit study (not a pure domain application): it uses Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and Qwen3.5-9B for test generation and rigorously dissects whether feedback-driven self-evolution gains are oracle artifacts. Strongly aligned with high-weight preferences (LLMs, code/programming, agents/self-evolution, evaluation). The freeze-then-audit protocol, candidate-budget matching, density-matched feedback placebo, cross-fitted real faults, and blinded human semantic audit (κ=.823) constitute an unusually rigorous, honestly-scoped design: pre-specified gates, disclosed protocol amendments, explicit 'qualification-amended' labeling, and refusal to overclaim (feedback effect left 'unresolved'). Quantitative results are consistent across seeds, metrics, and cohorts (gain inflation 9.46–14.85 pp; resampling beats mutation-based evolution by 6.01–18.83 pp in all 12 cells). Main weaknesses: generalizability limited to one model family and Python exact-output algorithmic tasks (acknowledged in Section 7), the flagship RQ6 feedback contrast is inconclusive/post-hoc/amended, and development cohorts were exposed. Reproducibility is strong via an anonymized replication package with SHA-256-locked artifacts. Novelty is solid but incremental in that it is a diagnostic protocol rather than a new capability or method.

primary_link.title: Auditing and Decomposing Feedback-Driven Evolution in LLM Test Generation under the Oracle Problem

radar.summary: Execution feedback is often treated as a self-verifying signal for improving LLM-generated tests. However, when generated inputs are executed on a single accepted program and its outputs are used as ground truth, invalid or underspecified inputs can create spurious fault detections and apparent evolutionary gains. We audit this failure mode in feedback-driven test generation using 142 development tasks, 114 locked external tasks, and 138 held-out tasks, with two code models, three seeds, and fau
radar.summary_zh: 本文針對大型語言模型（LLM）自動產生測試時的「測試預言」問題進行系統性稽核。常見捷徑是把產生的輸入交給一個通過測試的參考程式，並將其輸出視為真值，這會把超出規格的行為偽裝成錯誤偵測與演化進展。作者提出「先凍結後稽核」協定：先以單一參考程式選出測試，再由其他獨立通過的實作差異覆核，並比較真實的三輪執行回饋迴圈與密度匹配的安慰劑對照。實驗涵蓋142個開發、114個程序鎖定的外部，以及138個保留（held-out）但資格經修訂的任務，使用Qwen2.5-Coder-7B與Qwen3.5-9B兩個模型、三個種子。結果顯示：外部任務上模型預期輸出與多實作面板一致率僅27.79%與50.12%；單一參考會膨脹表面演化增益9.46至14.85個百分點；稽核後，等預算的獨立重抽樣比突變式演化好6.01至18.83個百分點。真實回饋與安慰劑差異僅+0.13與−0.50個百分點，保留群體上為+1.99與+0.28，皆未達預設等效或優越門檻；配對可用產量後對比轉為−0.30與+0.78且信賴區間跨零。雙盲語意審查判定94.41%遭面板否決的輸入無效，但3.60%有效，顯示面板不一致是證據而非語意定論。限制包括安慰劑屬事後設計、保留群體資格檢核經修訂，且兩模型同屬Qwen家族，整體屬診斷性證據而非乾淨的確證實驗。本文貢獻在於提供一套分離驗證器假象、互動鷹架與真實回饋貢獻的稽核協定，可作為未來回饋驅動測試演化研究的評估準則。
radar.title: Auditing and Decomposing Feedback-Driven Evolution in LLM Test Generation under the Oracle Problem
radar.title_zh: 在測試預言問題下對LLM測試產生的回饋驅動演化進行稽核與分解

links.title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing

evidence: Abstract: J64 adds 0.096-0.135 held-out AUC over a token-occupancy baseline aggregated identically; R64 reaches median per-axis correlation 0.69-0.86 across three models and two families and preserves 95-100% of J64's predictive gain on gpt-oss-20b.
Section 4.1 (RQ1): paired within-problem AUC increments from adding J64 to matched text model are +0.135* (Low), +0.129* (Medium), +0.096* (High), with 47x more features given to the text channel.

Section 4.2 (RQ2): median per-axis reconstruction 0.692-0.864 across eight model-effort settings; shuffled routing collapses to r~0; residualizing against token occupancy and log-length still yields additional held-out R2 of 0.082-0.085.

Section 5.1 / Table 1: cross-benchmark frozen transfer best-of-64 shows J64 +5.0 and +4.9 effort-averaged points over random pick on gpt-oss-20b and 120b, and R64-weighted voting improves majority voting in seven of eight settings.

Section 5.2 / Table 3: online stop-and-resample with nested operating-point selection; J64 beats sibling-permuted control by +1.3* to +5.9* points on gpt-oss-20b High and +0.9* to +1.7* on Qwen, with R64 retaining 0.9-3.2 points.

Section 5.3 / Table 7-8: router edits induce predicted behaviors (100 'Case n' headers vs 0 in 160 sham runs; accuracy 0.381 to 0.000; suppression shortens generations by 45.9 tokens* and replaces numerical guessing with symbolic derivation on one case study).

Section 6 (Limitations): authors state analysis centers on competition mathematics and gpt-oss-20b, frames are model-specific and not aligned across models, online control is evaluated mainly by causally masked replay, and interventions remain small.

Appendix B.1/B.3: full construction algorithm (Algorithm 1) with exact constants (lambda=50 ridge, C=3, 256-token windows, tau and K grids) and timing measurements (38.4 ms/token decode; 0.07/0.09 ms hook overhead), supporting reproducibility, though no explicit code release is claimed.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A methodology paper squarely in scope: it operationalizes a vocabulary-aligned internal readout (J64) of LLM reasoning state, reconstructs it from native MoE routing (R64), and uses it for test-time selection, online stop-and-resample control, and causal router edits on gpt-oss and Qwen3 reasoning models. Strong preference match to LLMs, reasoning/CoT, MoE architecture, interpretability, and test-time compute. Novelty is solid but derivative of the Jacobian lens (Gurnee et al.) and DeepConf baselines; the routing-only reconstruction and mechanism-matched interventions are the genuinely new contributions. Rigor is unusually high: matched token-occupancy baselines aggregated identically, sibling-permuted controls, frozen cross-benchmark transfer, nested operating-point selection to avoid test-set tuning, construction-disjoint checks, capacity-matched PCA control, and sham-edit controls for interventions, all with question-level clustered CIs. Evidence is extensive and internally consistent across three models, though effects are sometimes modest, the rescue slice is hindsight-selected (acknowledged), and benchmarks are small (30 questions each; 198 GPQA). Generalizability is limited: frames are model-specific and not aligned across models, evaluation centers on competition mathematics, and online control is mainly causally-masked replay rather than live serving, as the limitations section concedes. Reproducibility is good given Algorithm 1 and exact constants (lambda=50, C=3, 256-token windows, timing measurements), though no explicit code/data release is claimed.

primary_link.title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing

radar.summary: What a reasoning model writes is only a partial record of the process that produces it. We introduce a two-level internal readout for mixture-of-experts reasoning. We first distill vocabulary-scale J-space into J64, a 64-axis semantic frame learned from the model's own reasoning states. J64 reveals readable process state that the emitted trace does not show: it separates inference effort from problem-induced strain. It also adds 0.096 to 0.135 held-out AUC over a baseline that reads the same rol
radar.summary_zh: 推理模型寫出的思考軌跡只是其內部運作的部分紀錄。本文針對混合專家（MoE）推理模型提出兩層式內部讀出：先從模型自身的推理狀態，將詞彙規模的 J-space 提煉成 64 軸語意框架 J64，可讀出軌跡未顯示的過程狀態，並分離「推理力道」與「題目難度造成的負荷」兩個近乎正交的座標；相較於以 token 佔用率讀取同一 rollout 的對照基準，J64 在 held-out 評估上額外貢獻 0.096 至 0.135 的 AUC。作者再以原生專家路由統計透過 ridge 迴歸重建 J64，得到低開銷代理 R64：在三個模型、兩個家族上，各軸中位相關達 0.69 至 0.86，於 gpt-oss-20b 保留 J64 預測增益的 95% 至 100%。應用上，J64 與 R64 能改善已完成候選的單軌選擇，R64 加權投票在八分之七的設定中優於多數決；生成過程中以滾動視窗驅動的停止與重採樣策略，J64 相較兄弟置換對照提升 1.1 至 5.9 點，R64 保留其中 0.9 至 3.2 點；針對 J64 所指認機制的路由編輯亦誘發預期行為，將數值猜測轉為精確的符號推導。限制在於分析以競賽數學與 gpt-oss-20b 為主，各模型框架獨立建構、彼此不對齊，線上控制以因果遮蔽的重播評估，介入規模亦小。其價值在於讓潛藏的推理狀態既可解讀又可部署，為測試期算力分配提供可操作的遙測訊號。
radar.title: Beyond the Trace: Coupling an Interpretable Reasoning-State Readout to Native MoE Routing
radar.title_zh: 超越軌跡：將可解讀的推理狀態讀出與原生 MoE 路由耦合

links.title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists

evidence: §6 (Prospectively Specified Analyses): hypotheses were fixed before each wave (e.g., H2 predicted Copy R≥0.8 on shape-compatible hops); outcomes are reported against them, including refutations and a wave-5 correction overturning the wave-4 anneal/soup attribution.

§7.3 / Table 8: naive adapter copying collapses between independent pretraining runs (Banking77 Qwen2→2.5 R=−0.551, score .4286 vs floor .6071; OLMo-1→1.7 R=−0.32) but retains R=0.88/0.99 at a 46B-token OLMo continuation and falls to the floor (R=−0.02) at a 2.9T-token continuation, with anneal and soup edges adding no further damage.

§7.10 / Table 10: the pre-specified policy replayed over 33 episodes on held-out test-set halves attains 0.37pp mean regret with zero regression episodes at 15.6 GPU-h versus 47.7 for always-retrain; copy-if-shape baseline yields 17.11pp mean regret and 14 regressions.
§5 (Study inventory): 98 QLoRA trainings, 193 evaluation cells, 148.7 training GPU-hours with 47.8 kWh measured board energy, all on one RTX 4090 with pinned software versions.

§7.12 (Threats): authors state one lineage per family, one dataset per task class, QLoRA r=16 only with full fine-tuning unmeasured, and 1.8pp seed spread on the Spider/Qwen3 reference limiting single-hop retention arithmetic.

Reproducibility Statement: releases training/evaluation scripts, all 98 adapters, per-query records and bootstrap CIs for 193 cells, split manifests, relabeled Refresh-D corpora, memorization-probe outputs, and raw cost logs, 'to be released publicly upon publication'.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A decision-centric longitudinal benchmark measuring the freeze/port/refresh/retrain choice for fine-tuned LLM specialists across real Qwen and OLMo release lineages. Strongly aligned with core LLM preferences (LLMs, PEFT/QLoRA fine-tuning, evaluation/benchmarks, function calling, text-to-SQL, cost-aware serving); no Japanese or reasoning content. Methodological hygiene is unusually high: prospectively specified hypotheses with wave boundaries, paired exact McNemar tests, multi-seed checks that overturned a single-seed decline (CLINC150), artifact controls (template swap, bf16 re-run, constrained decoding), and explicit self-corrections. The continuity/distance porting criterion is the standout novel finding, replicated in two families, though it rests on few cells and endpoint-only distance sampling. Generalizability is limited by English-only tasks, one lineage per family, a single QLoRA r=16 recipe (rank dependence shown), and the 8B cap; reproducibility claims are extensive but public release is deferred to publication.

primary_link.title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists

radar.summary: Organizations maintain task-specific adapters for open-weight language models, and each new base-model release forces a migration decision: retain existing specialists, port adapters, refresh from preserved behavior, or retrain. Prior transfer work evaluates isolated model pairs, without studying these choices across real model release sequences. We present UpgradeBench, a decision-driven longitudinal benchmark covering four consecutive Qwen releases, one continuation checkpoint, six tasks, and
radar.summary_zh: 企業常在開源權重模型上微調出任務專用的 specialist，每當新基礎模型釋出，就面臨抉擇：凍結舊模型、移植 adapter、以舊模型為教師刷新，或全額重新訓練，但這個「升級稅」從未被系統性量測。作者提出 UpgradeBench，沿 Qwen1.5 到 Qwen3 四代、十四個月的完整釋出譜系，涵蓋六項任務與兩種規模（7–8B 與 1.5–1.8B），並以訓練譜系完全公開的 OLMo checkpoints 做前瞻式驗證；全部 98 次訓練在一張 RTX 4090 完成，並釋出逐題預測、成本與能源紀錄。核心發現：升級價值因任務而異——Banking77 凍結在九個 hop 保留 99–101% 效益，text-to-SQL 單次 hop 最多損失 59%；直接複製 adapter 的成敗不繫於架構相容，而繫於預訓練連續性：獨立預訓練的檢查點即使形狀相同也崩潰至低於不用 adapter 的水準，短程延續預訓練則保留 0.82–1.45，且可移植性隨延續距離衰減（46B tokens 保留 0.88–0.99，2.9T tokens 歸零）；以留存輸入做教師重新標註的 Refresh 達到與 gold-label 重訓相當的品質且零新增標註；預先指定的決策政策在 33 個升級情境上平均品質損失僅 0.37 個百分點、零行為退化，只花費三成的重訓運算與標註預算；CKA 探針可排序可移植性（Spearman 0.74）。限制包括僅測 QLoRA rank 16、模型規模上限 8B、任務皆為英文，且主要結論來自單一族系與固定資料集。此研究把升級決策變成可定價、可重播的問題，對企業維運 specialist 艦隊極具參考價值。
radar.title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists
radar.title_zh: UpgradeBench：以決策為核心、評估微調 LLM 專家模型升級的基準

links.title: Do LLMs Know What to Ask and When? Evaluating Multi-Turn Information Seeking

evidence: Abstract/Section 1: MT-InfoSeek instantiates a k-underspecified CSP formulation with 5,251 problems and 9,006 task instances spanning mathematics, logic, biology, medicine, and general knowledge.
Section 4, Takeaway 1/Fig. 3: k-prediction accuracy falls below 0.5 for k>=2, and at k=2 models predict a smaller k more than 4x as often as a larger one.

Appendix C.5: reruns under random and cooperative oracles confirm robustness - final sufficiency drops 29.7-41.9 pp (random) and 25.0-39.0 pp (cooperative) from k=1 to k=4 for four representative models.

Appendix C.6, Tables 4-10: LLM-based oracles (20Q, ClinGuide-MT) validated via 91.9-97.7% within-oracle consistency, 94.0% cross-oracle agreement, and human audits of 300 20Q questions and 200 ClinGuide oracle responses.

Appendix G.1.4, Table 22: prompt-perturbation study with problem-level cluster bootstrap (10,000 resamples, Holm correction) shows meaning-preserving reordering (P1) is within run-to-run noise for all tested models.
Appendix G.1.5, Table 23: force-ask intervention at k=3 raises final sufficiency by +25.7 pp for Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-FP8 (exact McNemar p<5e-4), with no significant effect for GPT-5-mini.

Appendix G.1.1/G.1.2: pooled fixed-effect regressions with interaction-clustered SEs show MSS relative mention rate predicts final sufficiency (beta_z=0.528, p=6.71e-45) while generic awareness does not (beta_z=0.005, p=0.853).
Appendix D, Table 11: per-dataset statistics given (e.g., Logic-Q-MT 600 problems/1200 tasks; GeneReg-MT 800 problems/2326 tasks; ClinGuide-MT 370 problems/1595 tasks).
Appendix E.2: open-weight models served with vLLM on H100 GPUs with documented tensor-parallelism, 131,072-token context, and FP8 KV cache settings.
Appendix A (Ethics statement): 'We have released code, data, and prompts to support reproducibility, auditing, and further stress-testing.'
Section 5 (Limitations): authors note equal-cost query assumption, LLM-based oracles for ClinGuide-MT/20Q, and that ClinGuide-MT 'does not establish clinical readiness.'
llm_evaluation.rationale: Strong preference match: an LLM-centric evaluation paper on multi-turn information seeking, intersecting LLMs, agents/tool-use-style interaction, reasoning (Logic-Q-MT, CoT trace analysis), and benchmark/evaluation methodology; the clinical and gene-regulation domains are evaluation substrates for LLM behavior rather than out-of-scope medical-AI or biology-foundation-model work. Novelty is solid but incremental: it extends QuestBench's k=1 CSP formulation to multi-turn k>1 with ground-truth MSSs and a 'final sufficiency' metric that separates acquisition from answering (Table 2 positions it as uniquely combining objective query labels, timing/order, and target control). Rigor is a standout: formal CSP definitions, adversarial/random/cooperative oracle robustness reruns (Appendix C.5), LLM-oracle reliability audits with human validation (Appendix C.6), prompt-sensitivity and MSS-resampling studies with cluster bootstrap and Holm correction (Appendix G.1.4, G.1.6), a force-ask intervention (Appendix G.1.5), and non-inferiority testing for first-turn-miss recovery. Evidence is quantitative and largely supports the takeaways (e.g., k-prediction accuracy <0.5 for k>=2 with >4x under-prediction at k=2; regression-adjusted CoT mention-rate effects), though some analyses rest on ~14-17 models and correlational comparisons, and a few models were run on reduced conditions. Generalizability is capped by the controlled setting: equal query costs, predefined queryable variables in structured domains, oracle-based rather than realistic user models - limitations the authors acknowledge in Section 5. Reproducibility is good: full prompts (Appendix E.1), vLLM serving details (Appendix E.2), dataset statistics (Table 11), and a stated release of code, data, and prompts (Appendix A).

primary_link.title: Do LLMs Know What to Ask and When? Evaluating Multi-Turn Information Seeking

radar.summary: When a user question is underspecified, a capable model should recognize that its context is insufficient, identify the missing information, ask for it, and respond only once that information determines a unique answer. We formalize multi-turn information seeking as solving a k-underspecified constraint satisfaction problem, where k is the number of variables jointly required to determine the target and therefore measures the degree of missing information. We instantiate the formulation in MT-In
radar.summary_zh: 哈佛大學團隊系統性評估大型語言模型（LLM）的多輪資訊尋求能力：當使用者問題欠明確（underspecified）時，理想模型應察覺脈絡不足並主動詢問缺少的資訊，直到該資訊足以唯一決定答案才回答。作者將此過程形式化為 k-欠明確約束滿足問題（k-underspecified CSP），k 為共同決定目標所需的最少變數數，並建構 MT-InfoSeek 評測套件，涵蓋數學、邏輯、生物、醫療與常識，共 5,251 個問題、9,006 個任務實例。評測分三軸：預測欠明確程度 k、辨識最小充分集合（MSS）、多輪循序互動解題，並以「最終充分性」（final sufficiency）區分資訊尋求與答案生成兩種能力。主要結果：模型能察覺資訊不足卻普遍低估其程度，在 k=2 邏輯題上低估約為高估的四倍；即使給定真實 k，仍難選出最小充分集合；互動常在資訊未充分時提前作答。隨 k 增大，成功更仰賴跨回合持續追問，首次提問失誤多可挽回；在講究順序依賴的臨床診斷任務（ClinGuide-MT）中，即使取得全部必要資訊，錯誤的提問順序仍會降低準確率；20Q 實驗顯示提問資訊量高不等於成功，證據整合能力同樣關鍵。限制：各提問皆視為等成本，ClinGuide-MT 與 20Q 由 LLM 擔任 oracle（經一致性與人工驗證），nEIG 指標依賴代理候選池，結果不代表臨床就緒。本研究指出最終準確率無法衡量互動素養，評測應記錄模型是否察覺資訊不足、需要哪些變數、以及是否確實透過多輪互動取得，MT-InfoSeek 提供了可控且具真值標註的評估框架。
radar.title: Do LLMs Know What to Ask and When? Evaluating Multi-Turn Information Seeking
radar.title_zh: LLM 知道該問什麼、何時提問嗎？——多輪資訊尋求能力評估

links.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution

evidence: Abstract: 'DeepSeek-V4-Flash surpasses GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), while the already strong GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2 points'; matches Table 3 (85.1 vs 76.0; 73.0 vs 68.7; 62.8->83.0).

Table 3 (Section 6.2): nine-benchmark averages rise 74.1->81.8 (+7.7) on GLM-5.2 and 66.7->75.5 (+8.8) on DeepSeek-V4-Flash; JIT-equipped systems best in 8 of 9 columns (counting the table confirms 7 for JIT+GLM-5.2 plus Shop for JIT+DeepSeek).

Table 4 (Section 6.3): backbone-fixed comparison vs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, NanoBot; JIT-Agent lowest tokens/cost in all six settings, e.g., DeepSeek-V4-Flash xBench-DS 527K->$0.075 drops to 212K->$0.039 while score rises 78.0->82.0.

Sections 4.1-4.3: full objective definitions for Stage I (SFT + length-normalized DPO variant with reward/latency/cost value gaps), Stage II (repair trajectories bounded at K*<=2), Stage III (Evo-GDPO with decoupled group normalization and PPO-style clipping).

Section 6.5 / Figure 5: 24 matched backbone-benchmark comparisons vs ReAct, average +7.6, but uses 100-example DeepSearchQA subset and 50-example subsets for the other benchmarks; no variance reported.
Section 6.6 / Figure 6: Streaming JIT beats Static JIT on three planning/workspace streams; only qualitative note that cost/tool traces are 'of broadly similar scale'.

Section 3.1 'Position' paragraph: authors concede production harnesses (Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness) are richer than the four-module instantiation; no dedicated limitations section elsewhere.

Front matter: GitHub (github.com/bingreeky/JIT), Hugging Face (JIT-Agent), and project website links provided; training hyperparameters, dataset sizes, teacher identity, and compute budget not reported in the document.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A core LLM-agent paper squarely matching top-weighted preferences (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, RL/alignment-flavored training). It trains a 27B meta-agent to synthesize, repair, and evolve four-module harnesses just-in-time, with a three-stage recipe (SFT + value-weighted DPO preference, bounded repair trajectories, Evo-GDPO). Quantitative claims are internally consistent (e.g., 85.1 vs GPT-5.6's 76.0 on DeepSearchQA = +9.1; Table 4 cost reductions 14.9-54.1% recompute correctly), with backbone-controlled harness comparisons, cost/token analysis, Pareto frontiers, 24 paired cross-family comparisons, and static-vs-streaming evolution. Deductions: no ablation isolating Stage I/II/III contributions or key hyperparameters (G, lambda_evo, weights), no statistical significance or variance on main tables (generalization uses 50-100 example subsets), no dedicated limitations section (only a 'Position' paragraph), vague training data sourcing and unreported hyperparameters/compute, and availability links (GitHub/HF) asserted but unverifiable from text. Novelty is moderate-good: the JIT Model-as-a-Harness framing and trained generator appear new, but it assembles known ingredients (ADAS/AFlow-style search, GDPO/GRPO, ReAct-style scaffolds) and its protocol is deliberately narrower than production harnesses.

primary_link.title: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution

top5.summary: Agent capability is not determined by the model alone. The agent harness, encompassing memory management, planning strategy, action protocol, and tool/skill orchestration, can dominate the contribution of the underlying foundation model. Yet harness design remains manual, task-specific, and fundamentally unscalable. We present JIT-Agent, a harness intelligence model trained to synthesize task-adaptive agent harnesses on the fly for arbitrary off-the-shelf agentic LLMs. We formalize the agent harness as a composable, machine-generatable artifact governed by a fixed four-module protocol, and train JIT-Agent to customize harnesses for a given task at hand, repair harnesses for stable and reliable execution, and self-evolve by distilling performance signals from an expanding archive of prior harness configurations. Equipped with JIT-Agent as a harness helper, DeepSeek-V4-Flash surpasses GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3), while the already strong GLM-5.2 gains up to +20.2 points. Across controlled evaluations, JIT-Agent-generated harnesses are performance-competitive with mature agent runtimes such as OpenCode and Claude Code and consistently improve multi-scale model families of DeepSeek V4, Mimo-V2.5, and Qwen3.6. To our knowledge, JIT-Agent is the first model purpose-built for just-in-time harness generation, establishing harness intelligence as a trainable, transferable, and compounding dimension of agent capability orthogonal to model scaling.
top5.summary_zh: 此論文指出 LLM 代理能力並非僅由模型權重決定，外部支架（harness，含記憶管理、規劃、動作協定與工具編排）常是成效關鍵，但支架設計仰賴人工、任務專用且難以擴展；既有方法多屬事先（AOT）最佳化，難以貼合個別任務。作者提出 JIT-Agent，訓練一個後設代理在推論當下為任意現成代理模型即時合成任務專屬支架。論文將支架形式化為固定四模組協定（記憶、規劃、動作、能力編排）下的可執行程式，並以 HarnessFactory 重新實作 13 種代表性 scaffold 作為種子庫；訓練分三階段：教師示範的客製化學習、將失敗生成轉為有限步修復軌跡的修復學習，以及 Evo-GDPO 線上策略最佳化，分別正規化獎勵、延遲與成本，鼓勵新支架超越現有檔案庫前沿。實驗顯示 DeepSeek-V4-Flash 搭配 JIT-Agent 在 DeepSearchQA 領先 GPT-5.6 達 9.1 分，GLM-5.2 在 DeepPlanning-Travel 提升 20.2 分；受控比較中與 Claude Code、OpenCode 等成熟執行環境相當或更佳，平均降低約 36% 每案例成本，且串流推論可持續從執行回饋演化檔案庫。限制包括四模組協定較產品級執行環境簡化、少數基準仍落後最佳固定支架，以及品質取決於協定與驗證器設計。此工作確立「支架智慧」為可訓練、可遷移、與模型規模正交的代理能力新維度。

links.title: Terminal Agents: A Survey of AI Agents in Command-Line Environments

evidence: Section 6.1: benchmark-exposure diagnostic fixes mini-SWE-agent with DeepSeek-V4-Flash across 241 Terminal-Bench 2.1, 93 SetupBench, 21 LongCLI-Bench, and 640 BashArena tasks; matched diagnostic covers 80 Claw-SWE-Bench Lite and 300 SWE-bench Lite tasks.
Section 6.1: 'Each task has one formal run per condition' — no repeated runs, limiting evidence strength.

Appendix C.3: P2/P4/P6 labels generated by DeepSeek-V4-Flash, the same model family as the agent under evaluation; the 0.7 confidence threshold is described as 'an engineering filter over the judge's reported confidence rather than a calibrated probability'.

Appendix C.6/C.7: none of six paired model-variant contrasts significant after Holm adjustment; Cochran's Q rejects equal system rates in all four blocks (Q=10.57 to 16.00), with benchmark-specific significant pairwise contrasts only.
Appendix C.4: LongCLI-Bench has 21 tasks with 68.7% episode-level coverage and 28.2% uncertainty; its auxiliary indicators are 'interpreted directionally'.
Appendix A.2: 'the iterative initial retrieval did not preserve a complete query-level candidate count before deduplication' — a documented gap in the search protocol.
Section 6.2/Table 4: P1 rule-matched invocation-failure rate rounds to 0.0% across all four benchmarks, interpreted as a narrow signal rather than evidence of flawless action formulation.

Abstract/Appendix A: public GitHub repository (awesome-terminal-agents) and supplementary protocol tables support corpus reproducibility, while trace-release policy for the paper's own diagnostics is discussed but not explicitly committed (Section 5.6).
llm_evaluation.rationale: A survey of LLM agents in terminal/command-line environments, squarely aligned with top-weighted preferences (agents/tool use, LLMs, coding agents, safety/governance, agent evaluation). Its substrate-centered scope tests and seven-dimensional competence profile are a genuinely fresh synthesis angle, and the fixed-condition diagnostics (benchmark-exposure and matched-system comparisons) add original empirical texture rare in surveys. Rigor is above average for a survey: documented review protocol, fixed decoding/seed/budgets, McNemar with Holm correction, Cochran's Q, and Wilson intervals. However, key weaknesses temper the score: only one formal run per condition; P2/P4/P6 process indicators are judged by DeepSeek-V4-Flash, the same model family as the evaluated agent, with the human audit described as qualitative only and without inter-rater statistics; LongCLI-Bench has only 21 tasks with 28.2% uncertainty; and the initial retrieval did not preserve query-level counts. Evidence claims are appropriately bounded ('in its reported setting'), but the empirical base is small and SWE-concentrated, limiting generalizability of the framework's cross-domain aspirations. Reproducibility is aided by a public corpus repo and unusually detailed appendix protocols (prompts, seeds, budgets), though trace release is discussed rather than committed and the judge model is proprietary.

Using terminal-mediated execution as an organizing lens, this survey establishes workload-level boundaries and connects
top5.summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）代理人日益透過終端機採取行動，但既有綜述將終端機媒介的行為分散於軟體工程、工具使用與電腦使用研究，缺乏統整觀點。本綜述以終端機媒介執行為組織主軸，將終端機代理人定義為任務進展主要依賴命令執行、文字回饋與具狀態環境互動的系統，提出三項 workload 層級的邊界測試，以及涵蓋命令制訂、回饋與產物解讀、執行環境管理、狀態與脈絡追蹤、進度驗證、復原調適、治理與副作用控制的七維能力輪廓，據此串聯系統架構（介面與觀察、執行環境與工作區、控制與治理、harness 與脈絡四層）、能力取得（可執行軌跡的蒐集、過濾與失敗資料）及評估（基準設計、證據層級與協定效度）。有界固定條件診斷顯示：固定組態下，不同基準家族揭露的過程訊號各異；在任務配對的系統比較中，SWE-agent 於四個區塊均居首，但 OpenHands 與 mini-SWE-agent 的相對排序隨基準翻轉，且模型變體差異皆未達統計顯著，凸顯元件歸因的困難。主要限制為證據集中於軟體工程領域、診斷屬單次有界快照、跨系統過程指標受介面差異影響。本文價值在於建立統一分析框架，呼籲明確揭露系統與執行條件、保留可重放軌跡與過程級證據，並指引跨領域能力、新鮮且可重放的過程評估、執行期治理與安全，以及模型–harness 歸因四大研究方向。

links.title: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use for Large Language Model Agents

evidence: Abstract: 'A 4B Qwen3 trained with SMITH on 13 procedural reasoning tasks with exact verifiers reaches 79.8 macro-average accuracy on held-out tasks... 40.4 on TabMWP-Hard and 42.6 on out-of-domain GQA (+7.6 over the best same-backbone inference-time baseline)'

Section 3.6 / Table 1: 'SMITH leads held-out generalization (RG Unseen 79.9) over distilled models (ReTool 63.2, LATM-distill 65.8)... using 32x fewer output tokens than standard CoT' (100 vs 3,206 output tokens)
Section 3.11 / Table 7: 'Decoupled build/use does not beat single-model Tool Create on RG (Unseen) (58.9 vs 68.8)... only the full SMITH objective wins on aggregate' (Full: RG S 86.61, RG U 78.33)
Section 3.9 / Table 5: 'for Qwen3-8B, SMITH improves... (72.6→79.4) and the holdout RG accuracy (72.2→81.7)... Granite-3.3-8B... lifts RG (Seen) to 39.1, RG (Unseen) to 28.5'
Section 3.7 / Table 3: 'the SMITH-4B-written tools lift the 30B consumer on every group, most sharply on TabMWP-Hard (0.7→38.8), and raise the task-weighted overall score from 70.2 to 76.6'
Section 3.10 / Table 6: 'SMITH lifts BFCL overall accuracy on both Qwen backbones, from 45.1 to 48.6 on Qwen3-4B and from 43.3 to 55.8 on Qwen3-8B'
Appendix B: documents a verifiable training failure ('naming drift' reward collapse, Table 8 per-step metrics) and derives five design lessons for verifier+judge reward combination

Section 4 Limitations: 'All trained policies are at most 8B parameters... whether the gains persist... at the 70B+ scale is an open question... we do not formally certify that adversarial prompts cannot induce unsafe tools'
Appendix N: 'All SMITH training runs were performed on a single NVIDIA RTX 6000 Pro GPU... between 36 and 72 hours'
Appendix O / Table 17: 'No configuration ever significantly outperforms v1' (two-sided exact McNemar tests), guarding against under-tuned-baseline objections

Inconsistency noted: Appendix I states 'ReTool achieves the highest in-distribution accuracy on RG (Seen) (92.0 vs. our 86.6)' while Section 3.6/Table 1 report 92.2 vs 85.2, and Appendix J reports LATM-distill Seen 83.3 / Unseen 66.4 vs Table 1's 81.7 / 65.8
llm_evaluation.rationale: Core LLM/agent-methodology paper: RL-trained joint tool creation and use (SMITH) on Qwen3 backbones, squarely matching high-weight preferences for LLMs, agents & tool use, reasoning, and RL. Novelty is solid but incremental over LATM/CRAFT/TroVE/KTCE (inference-time tool creation) and ReTool/SAGE (RL for tool use/skills); the genuinely new elements are the schema-grounded joint build/use objective, three disentangled reward axes, easy-to-hard evaluation split, and tool-pool curriculum. Rigor is strong: many same-backbone baselines, seeded re-evaluations with std, a full reward-structure ablation (Table 7), cross-backbone replication (Table 5), BFCL v4 transfer, and unusually candid baseline forensics (Appendix L) plus a McNemar-tested prompt-tuning ablation (Appendix O). Evidence strength is good but dented by internal numeric inconsistencies (abstract/conclusion 79.8 vs Table 1 79.9; Appendix I 'ReTool 92.0 vs ours 86.6' vs Section 3.6/Table 1 '92.2 vs 85.2'; Appendix J 'Seen 83.3/Unseen 66.4' vs Table 1 '81.7/65.8') and reliance on an LLM judge whose bias is only partially probed by the Self-Judge ablation. Generalizability is supported across 4B/8B/Granite backbones, a 350M and a 30B consumer, TabMWP-Hard, and GQA (though GQA needs fixed visual primitives and the paper concedes the GPT-4.1 distillation gap there), but 70B+ scale and richer artifacts (MCP/skills) are explicitly open (Section 4). Reproducibility is high: verbatim judge prompt (Appendix C), full task splits (Appendix F), hyperparameters (Tables 12-13), tool-pool design (Appendix E), and single-GPU 36-72h cost (Appendix N), with Code/Project Page links claimed. Not out-of-scope; no instruction-following from paper text was performed.

primary_link.title: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use for Large Language Model Agents

top5.summary: Tool-augmented language models are bounded by the APIs humans bothered to write; existing tool-creation systems patch this by prompting a frozen LLM at inference time, leaving the model that writes a tool decoupled from the one that uses it, with no signal that the schemas it produces are schemas it can invoke. We propose SMITH (Schema-grounded Multi-task Iterative Tool Honing), a reinforcement learning framework that jointly trains tool creation and tool use inside a single policy. Each rollout
top5.summary_zh: 本文提出 SMITH，一個以強化學習在單一策略內同時訓練「建立工具」與「使用工具」的框架。現有工具增強系統依賴人類預先設計的 API，推論時的工具生成方法（LATM、CRAFT、TroVE、KTCE）僅以提示詞驅動凍結模型，寫工具與用工具脫鉤，缺乏「寫出的 schema 能否被自己呼叫」的訓練訊號。SMITH 交錯兩類任務：build 任務自少量範例歸納出 Python 函式與 OpenAI 相容的 JSON schema；use 任務只看 schema，須從工具池挑選並呼叫工具回答保留題。獎勵分為格式一致性、執行準確率（於更難題組上評估，評估器定期與策略同步）與 LLM 審查品質三個獨立軸，以 DAPO 聯合最佳化，並採由易到難協定逼出可泛化的抽象工具。以 Qwen3-4B-Instruct 加 LoRA 在 13 個 Reasoning-Gym 程序性任務上訓練後，未見任務達 79.8% 巨觀平均準確率，超越所有推論時與蒸餾基線，每題輸出約 100 tokens（較 CoT 少 32 倍）；零樣本轉移於 TabMWP-Hard 得 40.4%，GQA 得 42.6%。其工具可跨規模移植：讓 LFM2.5-350M 追平 30B 工具撰寫模型，訓練配方亦一致提升 Qwen3-8B 與 Granite-3.3-8B，並改善 BFCL v4 外部工具呼叫。限制：模型規模至多 8B、依賴 30B LLM 審查、工具僅為單一函式與 schema、未觀察到平行工具呼叫，沙盒安全亦未正式驗證。此研究證明讓模型學會撰寫自己能可靠呼叫的工具，是邁向可重用、可遷移代理能力的可擴充路徑。
top5.title: Joint Optimization of Tool Creation and Use for Large Language Model Agents
top5.title_zh: 大型語言模型代理之工具建立與使用的聯合最佳化

links.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

evidence: Abstract: introduces Visual Rubrics-Based RL decomposing reference responses into atomic VF/RC/IF propositions for structured partial credit during post-training.
Section 4.3: rubric-based GRPO gives +1.79 Overall Avg. over answer-only GRPO on knowledge benchmarks (66.25 -> 68.04 via Table 3), with gains concentrated on MMMU/MMMU-Pro.
Section 4.3: 'scalar GRPO remains better on MathVerse V/O and CharXiv reasoning', so the improvement is not uniform across benchmarks.

Table 3 (Section 4.3 Ablations): answer-only 66.25, scalar sequence-level rubrics 67.74, component+prefix 68.04; the 0.30 gap jointly reflects component-wise standardization and localization, not localization alone.
Section 6 Limitations: admits judge-model family bias (Qwen-family judge scoring Qwen-family policy), approximate fuzzy-match prefix localization, and no large human-audited rubric evaluation.
Appendix C.3: 352,938 rubric items (209,436 VF, 101,369 RC, 42,133 IF) generated entirely by Gemini-3-Pro under one structured prompt; no human verification of rubric quality is reported.
Appendix D.2 Table 6: full GRPO configuration (verl Megatron backend, lr 2e-6, G=12 rollouts, KL 0.01, Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B as training judge), supporting reproducibility.
Appendix E: acknowledges weaker regimes (MMBench-Dev, MathVerse V/O, CharXiv) attributed to rubric-metric mismatch.
llm_evaluation.rationale: A VLM post-training methodology paper (rubric-based rewards for GRPO on Qwen3-VL-8B), squarely within the Multimodal AI, Alignment/RLHF, Reasoning, and LLM-as-judge preferences; not pure computer vision and not out of scope. Novelty is incremental: it extends Rubrics-as-Rewards (Gunjal et al., 2025, cited in Section 2) to visually grounded VF/RC/IF criteria, with prefix-localized credit as the main new mechanism. Rigor is moderate: fair shared-SFT/shared-data comparisons, a credit-assignment ablation (Table 3: 66.25 vs 67.74 vs 68.04), and detailed configuration, but single-seed runs, no significance testing, small deltas (0.30 between rubric variants, 1.79 over answer-only on knowledge Overall Avg.), and mixed per-benchmark results (Section 4.3 concedes scalar GRPO wins on MathVerse V/O and CharXiv). Evidence is quantitative but weakened by fully automatic Gemini-3-Pro rubric annotation with no human audit and same-family judge bias, both acknowledged in Section 6. Generalizability is limited to one backbone family with transfer explicitly left to future work. Reproducibility is relatively strong (hyperparameters in Appendix D.2 Table 6, data inventory in Table 4, judge prompts in Table 5, project page), though proprietary annotation models are a barrier.

primary_link.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning

top5.summary: Vision-language models can produce fluent answers that are insufficiently grounded in the visual evidence: a single unsupported object, chart value, or intermediate inference can undermine an otherwise plausible response. We argue that this is a credit-assignment failure in multimodal post-training. Scalar outcome rewards indicate whether an answer is acceptable, but do not identify which visual facts are grounded, which reasoning steps are valid, or which instruction constraints are missed. We introduce Visual Rubrics-Based Reinforcement Learning, which decomposes reference responses into atomic propositions and scores generated answers along Visual Faithfulness (VF), Reasoning Consistency (RC), and Instruction Following (IF). The resulting rubric items provide structured partial credit and localize rubric credit when supporting evidence spans are available. We first obtain an SFT checkpoint by fine-tuning Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on the public OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K corpus, adapting OpenMMReasoner's cold-start data recipe. We construct V-Rubrics 50K, a 50,248-example training set from 17 visually grounded sources, by applying rule-based filters before deriving example difficulty from rejection-sampling scores and then annotating every example with Gemini-3-Pro under the same structured prompt and protocol. We train our model based on the same SFT checkpoint using component-wise, prefix-localized rubric credit. Experiments show that our rubricbased GRPO improves over both the shared SFT baseline and answer-only GRPO, with the largest gains on knowledge-oriented and visually grounded reasoning benchmarks. The results show rubrics as a useful reward abstraction for visual post-training.
top5.summary_zh: 視覺語言模型（VLM）常生成流暢卻缺乏影像證據支持的回答，一個無根據的物件、圖表數值或推理步驟便足以破壞整體答案。本文將此視為多模態後訓練中的信用分配（credit assignment）問題：純量結果獎勵只能判斷答案對錯，無法指出哪些視覺事實有依據、哪些推理步驟失效。作者提出視覺評分規準強化學習（Visual Rubrics-Based RL），將參考回答分解為原子命題，並依視覺忠實性（VF）、推理一致性（RC）與指令遵循（IF）三個維度逐項評分。團隊建立 V-Rubrics 50K 資料集，含 50,248 筆來自 17 個視覺任務來源的範例，由 Gemini-3-Pro 依統一協定標註，訓練時以 Qwen3-VL-235B 擔任評審。模型先以 OpenMMReasoner-SFT-874K 微調 Qwen3-VL-8B，再用 GRPO 進行元件式、前綴局部化的規準信用訓練。實驗顯示，規準式 GRPO 在通用與知識基準的總平均達 68.04，優於僅用答案獎勵的 66.25 與 SFT 基線；在 MMMU、MathVision、DynaMath、WeMath、LogicVista 等依賴有據中間推理的任務增益最大，消融實驗亦支持元件加前綴設計優於序列層級彙總。限制方面：規準品質依賴自動生成與評審驗證、前綴定位採模糊比對僅屬近似，且同家族評審可能引入偏誤。此研究將視覺忠實性從事後評估診斷轉化為可操作的訓練介面，顯示評分規準是視覺後訓練中細粒度獎勵的有效抽象。
top5.title: V-Rubrics: Visual Faithfulness via Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
top5.title_zh: V-Rubrics：以評分規準強化學習實現視覺忠實性

evidence: Abstract: 'only 28 of 520 runs (5.4%) pass all three stages, 13 of the 20 tasks receive no accepted solution, and the best model (claude-opus-5) scores 47.0/100'

Section 2.1 'Why behavioural tests fail here': 'rate(R_A;T)=1 for any T—by construction... Setting R_S=R_A (the empty diff) therefore earns full marks on any behavioural suite' — formalizes the Blindness claim
Section 2.3 Scoring, Eq. (4): composite score defined as veto × all-or-nothing Stage II × (0.4 + 0.6·s/6) Stage III per-verifier factor
Section 3.4.1: 'Judge and human agree 89.7% of the time (140/156, κ=0.795)... of the 16 disagreements, 14 are the judge being too strict'

Section 3.3.2: 'Among the 340 runs that passed Stage I... 58% reach 99% and 36% reach 99.9%—but only 26% make no error at all' with concrete failure cases (fw03 hash routing 21768/21769, build03 wheel METADATA 380/381)

Section 3.4.3 Finding 1: 'the two held by claude-opus-5 are 55.7% and 53.4%, the other four between 21.6% and 26.1%... retire the two strongest and the remaining four would accept 46 submissions instead of 28'
Table 1 / Appendix C Table 10: 20 tasks, 130,118 fixed checks, 262 criteria, per-task versions, LoC, and time budgets listed
Section 1 (scoping limitation): 'these results establish a capability gap on the 20 tasks in SWE Refactor Bench; they do not rank the intrinsic difficulty of all migration projects'

Reproducibility gap: homepage URL given in metadata, but the paper text nowhere states code or task images will be publicly released; Stage I judge is gpt-5.6-sol (Section 3.4.1) and Stage III 'tests... vary across verifier runs' (Section 1)
llm_evaluation.rationale: Highly relevant to core preferences: an LLM coding-agent evaluation benchmark (Agents & Tool Use, LLMs, Code & Programming, Red Teaming & Evaluation). Novelty is solid: the identified 'Blindness' failure mode (Section 2.1 shows rate(R_A;T)=1 by construction for untouched repos) and the three-stage protocol with a Migration Audit veto plus Agentic Verification via executable counterexamples (Section 2.3, Eq. 4) are genuinely distinct from red-to-green suites like SWE-bench (Table 7). Rigor is strong: 520 runs over 8 models/26 configurations, an explicit scoring formula, funnel decomposition that is internally consistent (340/118/88/28, 30 blindness, 252 behavior-breaking), and a dedicated validity section including human-judge agreement (κ=0.795, Section 3.4.1) and family-bias controls (Section 3.4.3). Evidence is detailed (per-task Tables 9-10, concrete counterexample cases in 3.3.2/3.4.2, cost data in Table 3) but weakened by single-run-per-configuration sampling with no variance estimates and a small task set (20 tasks; platform and toolchain classes have only 3 tasks each, so category-difficulty claims rest on thin counts, acknowledged in Section 1). Generalizability is moderate: conclusions are scoped to these 20 tasks and the verifier panel is explicitly non-stationary ('retire the two strongest and the remaining four would accept 46 submissions instead of 28', Section 3.4.3). Reproducibility is partial: a homepage and a meticulous task catalogue with versions, licences, budgets and a construction procedure (Appendix A-C) are given, but no explicit code/data release statement appears in the text, and both the Stage I judge and verifiers rely on proprietary models with inherently variable Stage III output.

primary_link.title: SWE Refactor Bench: Can Coding Agents Complete a Long-Horizon, Whole-Repository Stack Migration?

top5.summary: Modern software systems accumulate technical debt over decades of development, which makes migration expensive and largely manual. As coding agents become increasingly capable at bug fixing, can they autonomously perform such migrations? Existing benchmarks cannot answer this question because they evaluate only behavioural correctness, not whether the migration actually occurred. This leads an easy hack: agents copy the original implementation to make tests pass. We call this Blindness. To address this problem, we introduce SWE Refactor Bench, a benchmark comprising 20 whole-repository migrations, covering 4 kinds of technical debt. A three-stage evaluation protocol measures both migration completeness and behavioural correctness. (1) Migration Audit verifies that the migration occurred. (2) Behavioural Tests measure correctness with a fixed test suite. (3) Agentic Verification uses 6 independent coding agents to generate targeted tests for hidden behavioural differences. Across 520 runs from 8 frontier models and 26 model-effort configurations, only 28 of 520 runs (5.4%) pass all three stages, 13 of the 20 tasks receive no accepted solution, and the best model (claude-opus-5) scores 47.0/100. Migration completeness and behavioural correctness are distinct abilities: a few runs preserve behaviour by skipping the migration and are stopped at Migration Audit; most attempt it and break behaviour, and are stopped at Behavioural Tests. Agents cannot deliver a perfect migration: among the 340 runs that pass Migration Audit, 58% reach 99% of the fixed checks, yet only 26% reach 100%. Agent capability differs across migration categories: agents score 31.4 on build toolchain rewrites but only 5.6 on language rewrites. Together, these findings position SWE Refactor Bench as a rigorous testbed for developing coding agents for reliable whole-repository migrations.
top5.summary_zh: 本論文探討編碼代理(coding agents)能否自主完成整個儲存庫的行為保持式技術堆疊遷移。現有基準僅以固定測試衡量行為正確性,但遷移任務起點的測試本就全數通過,代理照抄原實作也能拿滿分,作者稱此漏洞為 Blindness。為此團隊建立 SWE Refactor Bench:20 個取自真實開源基礎設施的整庫遷移任務(如 SQLite、zlib、GraphHopper),涵蓋語言、框架、平台與建置工具鏈四類技術債,並採三階段評測:遷移稽核以三取二多數決驗證遷移是否真的發生並握有否決權;行為測試要求 130,118 項固定檢查全數通過;代理驗證則由六個獨立編碼代理各花一小時搜尋差異,僅接受可執行的反例。在 8 個前沿模型、26 種組態共 520 次執行中,僅 28 次(5.4%)通過全部三階段,20 個任務有 13 個無人解出,最佳的 claude-opus-5 得分 47.0/100。「完成遷移」與「保持行為」是兩種不同能力:30 次執行跳過遷移卻保住行為,252 次完成遷移卻破壞行為;通過稽核的 340 次中僅 26% 全數通過固定檢查,而通過前兩階段的 88 個提交又有 60 個被驗證代理找出反例。類別間能力亦有差異:建置工具鏈改寫得分 31.4,語言改寫僅 5.6。限制上,結論僅針對這 20 個任務,不代表所有遷移專案的內在難度排序;評審與驗證代理的強度也會影響分數,且隨模型進步,同一任務集將被更嚴格評分。此基準為發展可靠的整庫遷移代理提供嚴謹的測試場域,並點出行為測試無法證明遷移確實發生的根本盲點。
